_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: Searching for an emoji and clicking it sets Shelley's favicon. The server's favicon emoji is 🐙. "The picker" is the dialog whose accessible name is "Favicon emoji"; "the favicon" is the element link[rel="icon"]. Call "puts" lists, as a JSON array, the emojis the page has asked the server to save. To "open the picker": press_key "k" with modifiers "Control" (on whatever has focus); fill ".command-palette-input" with "favicon emoji"; click the first ".command-palette-item"; then the picker should be visible. "The search box" is the picker's input[type=search]; it sits inside the emoji-picker element's shadow root, which CSS selectors cannot reach, so pick it as the element with role "combobox" and accessible name exactly "Search" (exact), with "within" the picker. An "option" is an element with role "option" inside the picker. To "type" text means a type step, with no click first: the keys go to whatever has focus. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /new. 2. [data-testid="message-input"] should be visible. 3. Open the picker. 4. Typing searches straight away once the picker has loaded: the search box must have focus. 5. The favicon's href attribute must be exactly {{OCTOPUS}}. 6. Type "fox". 7. Click the option whose accessible name contains "fox". 8. The picker should become hidden. 9. The favicon's href must be exactly {{FOX}}. 10. Call "puts": it must return exactly ["🦊"].
